title: The FIFO Fridge
sendTrigger: Send this to whoever cleans out the fridge.
editorialNotes: 20-30% FIFO waste-reduction figure and the $580-870/year applied estimate are foodservice benchmarks applied to average household spend, not a household-specific study - kept as a Steel Blue (savings, positive) hero number per the brief, never Signal Red since nothing here is a loss figure.

thread.element: small fridge icon reorganizing from chaos to order
thread.endState: clean FIFO-rotated fridge with a green check

copy.headline: Every restaurant in the world uses this system. Almost no home kitchen does.
copy.body: A clean, organized walk-in cooler versus a typical home fridge - everything shoved in, things hidden behind other things.

copy.headline: It's FIFO. First In, First Out.
items: New items go to the back.
Older items move to the front.
copy.body: You always use the oldest food first.

copy.headline: Restaurants use FIFO to cut food waste.
copy.body: Applied to a home kitchen, it saves money every year - from 30 seconds of effort per grocery trip.

copy.headline: The reason you don't do this already
items: Old food is "still fine." By the time "still fine" becomes "not fine," you can't see it anymore.

copy.headline: The cheapest upgrade to your kitchen isn't an appliance. It's putting old food in front of new food.
copy.ctaLine: fond tracks dates for you - but FIFO costs $0. Start today.
